bug.title: The public appeal detail leaks the opening of the hidden post, or the still-sealed review report, that the appeal is about
bug.symptoms: GET /v1/appeals/{cid} needs no token (appeals/router.py get_appeal_detail: "any reader may see it"), and it returns excerpt and target_link built by appeals/subject.py describe_subject, which calls moderation/outcomes.excerpt(): the first characters of a discussion post's text or a formal review's report, read straight from the ledger with no check of moderation hides or of the version's report gate So anyone who knows an appeal id reads the opening of the post a moderator hid; for an appeal on a decision about a formal review, the excerpt shows the report before reviews/history.py report_gate_open would serve it ("a sealed report stays out") Found by an automated security review of 895dc62 (Appeal polish), 2026-11-18
bug.reproduction_steps: 1. As a tier-4 moderator, hide a discussion post (moderation decision with action hide) 2. As the post's author, file an appeal on that decision and note the appeal cid 3. With no Authorization header, GET /v1/appeals/{appeal_cid}: excerpt holds the hidden post's text and target_link points at it 4. Repeat with a decision about a formal review on a version whose report gate is still closed: excerpt holds the sealed report's text
bug.expected: excerpt and target_link are filled only for a caller who may judge or contest the decision: a member seated on the appeal's panel, a tier-4 moderator, or the appellant; for every other caller, including a caller with no token, both are null. Whatever the caller, a formal review's report excerpt is withheld while that version's report gate is closed unless the caller is a tier-4 moderator or the review's author. API tests cover an anonymous reader, an unrelated signed-in reader, a seated member, a moderator and the appellant, for a hidden post and for a sealed review
bug.actual: Every reader, signed in or not, gets the excerpt and link of hidden content and of sealed review reports

constraints.constraint: The appeal itself stays a public record: id, decision, appellant, grounds, status, filed date, outcome and resolution are returned to every reader as today; target_cid, target_kind, record_type, paper_title and decision_action stay public because the public decision record already names them
Panel visibility (panel, viewer_on_panel, viewer_vote) keeps its current rules
